exposure: Emergency cesarean section (compared to elective cesarean section)
History of more than one prior cesarean section
outcome: Maternal outcomes (e.g., intraoperative hemorrhage, packed red blood cell transfusions, ascending branch ligation of the uterine artery)
Neonatal outcomes (e.g., neonatal intensive care unit admissions, birth weight)
cohort: The study included patients with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) who underwent cesarean section at three tertiary hospitals between January 2016 and January 2023.
finding: Emergency cesarean section in PAS patients is associated with increased transfusion requirements and adverse neonatal outcomes, with risk factors for emergency C-section including prior C-sections, low hemoglobin, preeclampsia, and vascular lacunae.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean section, compared to elective cesarean section, in PAS patients leads to significantly more packed red blood cell transfusions, higher rates of ascending branch ligation of the uterine artery, more neonatal intensive care unit admissions, and lower neonatal birth weight.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome, with neonates from emergency cesarean sections having lower birth weight.
